source.text: Ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις πάλιν πολλοῦ ὄχλου ὄντος καὶ μὴ ἐχόντων τί φάγωσιν, προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς λέγει αὐτοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: In those the days again great crowd being and not having what they might eat, having called to [him] the disciples he says to them,

en.L: In those days, when again [there] was a great crowd and they had nothing to eat, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called the disciples to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] and says to them,
en.B: During those days a large crowd had gathered again, and there was no food for them. So Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said to them,
en.R: Around that time another big crowd came together around Jesus. The people had run out of food. So Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers over and said to them,

es.L: En aquellos días, como de nuevo había una gran multitud y no tenían qué comer, habiendo llamado a los discípulos, les dice:
es.B: Por aquellos días se había juntado otra vez una gran multitud, y no tenían nada que comer. Entonces Jesús llamó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y les dijo:
es.R: Por ese tiempo se juntó otra gran multitud alrededor de Jesús. La gente se había quedado sin comida. Entonces Jesús llamó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y les dijo:

sw.L: Katika siku zile, kulipokuwa tena na umati mkubwa, nao hawakuwa na kitu cha kula, akiisha kuwaita wanafunzi, anawaambia,
sw.B: Siku hizo umati mkubwa ulikuwa umekusanyika tena, nao hawakuwa na chakula. Basi Yesu aliwaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, akawaambia,
sw.R: Wakati huo umati mwingine mkubwa ulikusanyika karibu na Yesu. Watu walikuwa wameishiwa chakula. Basi Yesu aliwaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akawaambia,

decisions.choice: again a great crowd: a second large crowd, like the one in 6:34
decisions.reason: The word for again points back to the earlier feeding. Mark tells a second, similar meal in a different place, the Gentile region of the Ten Towns where Jesus was in 7:31.

decisions.choice: again a great crowd, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read a single word meaning a very great crowd, without again. The SBLGNT reads again with great, as the older manuscripts do. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past, here and in 8:6, 8:12, 8:17, 8:19-20, 8:22, 8:29 and 8:33.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dice); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (dijo)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells a past event in the present (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same through the chapter.

decisions.choice: discípulos at every level
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "followers", Spanish keeps "discípulos", a common word every reader knows, as in John. The same through the chapter.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anawaambia); past at Balanced and Readable (akawaambia)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells a past event in the present (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same through the chapter.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi at every level
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "followers", Swahili keeps "wanafunzi", the everyday word for a teacher's disciples, as in John. The same through the chapter.

source.text: Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν·

records.literal_gloss: I have compassion on the crowd, because already days three they remain with me and not they have anything they might eat;

en.L: "I have compassion on the crowd, because they have already remained with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three days and do not have anything to eat;
en.B: "My heart goes out to these people. They have been with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for three days now, and they have nothing left to eat.
en.R: "I feel sorry for these people. They have stayed with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for three days, and now they have nothing to eat.

es.L: «Siento compasión por la multitud, porque ya hace tres días que permanecen conmigo y no tienen qué comer;
es.B: «Me conmueve profundamente esta gente. Ya llevan tres días conmigo y no les queda nada que comer.
es.R: «Siento lástima por esta gente. Llevan tres días aquí conmigo, y ahora no tienen nada que comer.

sw.L: "Ninauhurumia umati, kwa sababu tayari ni siku tatu wamekaa {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, wala hawana chochote cha kula;
sw.B: "Moyo wangu unawaonea huruma watu hawa. Sasa ni siku tatu wamekuwa {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, na hawana chakula kilichobaki.
sw.R: "Ninawasikitikia watu hawa. Wamekaa {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} kwa siku tatu, na sasa hawana chochote cha kula.

decisions.choice: have compassion: be moved deep inside with pity
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for the inner parts, where people felt strong feeling. It is used of Jesus at 1:41 and at the first feeding (6:34).

decisions.choice: already three days: they have stayed so long that their food is gone
decisions.reason: The point is how long they have kept listening to him in a lonely place.

decisions.choice: my heart goes out to
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a natural English phrase for deep pity.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on conmigo; spans only on separate pronouns and possessives (sus, le, lo, él, mí)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish joins some pronouns to a verb or preposition ("conmigo", "reprenderlo") and usually leaves the subject pronoun out, so there is nothing separate to capitalise. Spanish therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun span on the free pronoun nami; none on verb prefixes
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili carries most pronouns in the verb (-m- in "walimjibu"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives (nami, wake, yangu, yeye). Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἀπολύσω αὐτοὺς νήστεις εἰς οἶκον αὐτῶν, ἐκλυθήσονται ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ· καί τινες αὐτῶν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἥκασιν.

records.literal_gloss: and if I send away them hungry to [the] home of them, they will faint on the road; and some of them from far away have come.

en.L: and if I send them away hungry to their homes, they will faint on the road; and some of them have come from far away."
en.B: Send them home without food, and they will collapse on the road. Some of them have traveled a long way."
en.R: If they have to go home hungry, they will become weak and fall down on the way. Some of them have come from far away."

es.L: y si los despido hambrientos a su casa, desfallecerán por el camino; y algunos de ellos han llegado de lejos».
es.B: Si los mando a sus casas sin comer, se desplomarán por el camino. Algunos de ellos han venido de muy lejos».
es.R: Si tienen que irse a casa con hambre, se van a debilitar y se caerán por el camino. Algunos de ellos han venido desde lejos».

sw.L: na nikiwaruhusu waende nyumbani kwao wakiwa na njaa, wataishiwa nguvu njiani; na wengine wao wamekuja kutoka mbali."
sw.B: Nikiwaruhusu waende nyumbani bila kula, wataanguka njiani. Baadhi yao wamesafiri kutoka mbali sana."
sw.R: Wakienda nyumbani wakiwa na njaa, watachoka na kuanguka njiani. Baadhi yao wamekuja kutoka mbali."

decisions.choice: faint: give out from weakness and hunger
decisions.reason: The verb means to become slack or exhausted.

decisions.choice: from far away: perhaps a hint that Gentiles are among the crowd
decisions.reason: The scene is in Gentile country (7:31), and in the Scriptures those far off can mean the nations (Joshua 9:6; Isaiah 60:4). Mark may mean no more than the distance.

decisions.choice: and some of them, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts join the clause with a word meaning for, making it a reason. The sense is close either way. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

source.text: καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι Πόθεν τούτους δυνήσεταί τις ὧδε χορτάσαι ἄρτων ἐπ’ ἐρημίας;

records.literal_gloss: And answered him the disciples of him that, From where these will be able anyone here to satisfy with bread in a desolate place?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "From where will anyone be able to satisfy these [people] with bread here in a desolate place?"
en.B: His disciples replied, "Out here in this empty country, where could anyone find bread enough to fill all these people?"
en.R: His followers answered, "We are far from any town. How could anyone get enough bread here to feed all these people?"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿De dónde va a poder alguien hartar de pan a estos, aquí en un lugar despoblado?».
es.B: Sus discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} contestaron: «Aquí, en este lugar tan apartado, ¿dónde podría alguien conseguir pan suficiente para llenar a toda esta gente?».
es.R: Sus discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «Estamos lejos de cualquier pueblo. ¿Cómo podría alguien conseguir aquí pan suficiente para dar de comer a toda esta gente?».

sw.L: Na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimjibu, "Kutoka wapi mtu yeyote ataweza kuwashibisha hawa kwa mikate, hapa mahali pasipo na watu?"
sw.B: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimjibu, "Huku nyikani, mtu angeweza kupata wapi mikate ya kutosha kuwashibisha watu wote hawa?"
sw.R: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimjibu, "Tuko mbali na mji wowote. Mtu angewezaje kupata mikate ya kutosha hapa kuwalisha watu wote hawa?"

decisions.choice: desolate place: open country far from towns
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the lonely place of the first feeding (6:35). It recalls Israel fed in the wilderness (Exodus 16).

decisions.choice: a question that sees no way to feed them
alternatives: a request for Jesus to act
decisions.reason: The disciples have seen the first feeding (6:35-44), yet they speak as though they had not. Jesus takes this up in 8:17-21.

decisions.choice: we are far from any town
decisions.reason: Readable says what the lonely place means for the problem.

source.text: καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτούς· Πόσους ἔχετε ἄρτους;

records.literal_gloss: And he was asking them, How many have you loaves?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "How many loaves do you have?"
en.B: He asked them, "How many loaves have you got?"
en.R: Jesus asked them, "How many loaves of bread do you have?"

es.L: Y les preguntó: «¿Cuántos panes {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}?».
es.B: Les preguntó: «¿Cuántos panes {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}?».
es.R: Jesús les preguntó: «¿Cuántos panes {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}?».

sw.L: Naye akawauliza, "Mna mikate mingapi?"
sw.B: Aliwauliza, "Mna mikate mingapi?"
sw.R: Yesu aliwauliza, "Mna mikate mingapi?"

decisions.choice: loaves: small flat rounds of bread
decisions.reason: Bread was baked in small, flat rounds, one or two of which made a meal for a person.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} and every plural "you" in the chapter
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" (the default) and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἑπτά.

records.literal_gloss: And they said, Seven.

en.L: And they said, "Seven."
en.B: "Seven," they answered.
en.R: They said, "Seven."

es.L: Y ellos dijeron: «Siete».
es.B: «Siete», respondieron.
es.R: Ellos dijeron: «Siete».

sw.L: Nao wakasema, "Saba."
sw.B: "Saba," walijibu.
sw.R: Walisema, "Saba."

decisions.choice: seven: a number of fullness
alternatives: a count with no further meaning
decisions.reason: The first feeding began with five loaves and ended with twelve baskets. Here there are seven loaves and seven baskets (8:8). Seven can stand for completeness, but Mark gives no explanation.

source.text: καὶ παραγγέλλει τῷ ὄχλῳ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν καὶ παρέθηκαν τῷ ὄχλῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And he directs the crowd to recline on the ground; and having taken the seven loaves, having given thanks he broke and was giving to the disciples of him that they might set before, and they set before the crowd.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} directs the crowd to recline on the ground; and having taken the seven loaves [and] given thanks, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke [them] and was giving [them] to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples so that they would serve [them], and they served the crowd.
en.B: He had the crowd sit on the ground. Taking the seven loaves, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave thanks, broke them, and kept handing them to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to pass around, and they served them to the crowd.
en.R: Jesus told the people to sit on the ground. He took the seven loaves and thanked God for them. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the bread into pieces and gave it to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to hand out. They gave it to the people.

es.L: Y manda a la multitud recostarse en el suelo; y tomando los siete panes [y] dando gracias, [los] partió y [los] iba dando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos para que [los] sirvieran, y [los] sirvieron a la multitud.
es.B: Mandó a la gente que se sentara en el suelo. Tomó los siete panes, dio gracias, los partió y se los iba dando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos para que los repartieran; y ellos los repartieron entre la gente.
es.R: Jesús le dijo a la gente que se sentara en el suelo. Tomó los siete panes y le dio gracias a Dios por ellos. Después partió el pan en pedazos y se lo dio a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos para que lo repartieran. Ellos se lo dieron a la gente.

sw.L: Naye anauagiza umati uketi chini; na akiisha kuichukua ile mikate saba [na] kushukuru, akaimega, akawa akiwapa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ili waigawe, nao wakaugawia umati.
sw.B: Aliuagiza umati uketi chini. Kisha akaichukua ile mikate saba, akashukuru, akaimega, akawa akiwapa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waigawe; nao wakaugawia umati.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia watu waketi chini. Akaichukua ile mikate saba, akamshukuru Mungu kwa ajili ya mikate hiyo. Kisha akaimega vipande vipande, akawapa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waigawe. Nao wakawagawia watu.

decisions.choice: recline: sit or lie down to eat
decisions.reason: People lay or sat on the ground for a meal, as at the first feeding (6:39-40).

decisions.choice: took, gave thanks, broke, gave: the same actions as at the Last Supper
decisions.reason: Mark uses the same series of verbs at the first feeding (6:41) and at the Last Supper (14:22-23). The word for giving thanks is the one used of the cup at 14:23.

decisions.choice: was giving: he kept handing the bread out
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes repeated action as the bread kept coming.

decisions.choice: thanked God for them
decisions.reason: Readable names God, to whom the thanks were given.

source.text: καὶ εἶχον ἰχθύδια ὀλίγα· καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτὰ εἶπεν καὶ ταῦτα παρατιθέναι.

records.literal_gloss: And they had small fish a few; and having blessed them he said also these to be set before.

en.L: And they had a few small fish; and having blessed them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to serve these also.
en.B: They also had a few small fish. He blessed them and told the disciples to hand those out too.
en.R: They also had a few small fish. Jesus thanked God for the fish and told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to give them out too.

es.L: Y tenían unos pocos pescaditos; y habiéndolos bendecido, dijo que se sirvieran también estos.
es.B: Tenían también unos cuantos pescaditos. Los bendijo y dijo a los discípulos que los repartieran también.
es.R: También tenían unos pocos pescados pequeños. Jesús le dio gracias a Dios por los pescados y les dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos que también los repartieran.

sw.L: Nao walikuwa na visamaki vichache; naye akiisha kuvibariki, akasema na hivyo pia vigawiwe.
sw.B: Walikuwa pia na visamaki vichache. Alivibariki, akawaambia wanafunzi wavigawe navyo pia.
sw.R: Walikuwa pia na samaki wadogo wachache. Yesu alimshukuru Mungu kwa ajili ya samaki hao, akawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wawagawe pia.

decisions.choice: blessed them: gave thanks to God over the fish
decisions.reason: In a Jewish blessing at a meal, God is praised for the food. To bless the food means to give thanks for it.

decisions.choice: small fish: little fish, perhaps dried or salted
decisions.reason: The word is a diminutive. Small fish were often dried or pickled around the lake.

decisions.choice: thanked God for the fish
decisions.reason: Readable says what blessing the food means, as in 8:6.

source.text: καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ἦραν περισσεύματα κλασμάτων ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας.

records.literal_gloss: And they ate and were satisfied, and they took up left over of broken pieces seven large baskets.

en.L: And they ate and were satisfied, and they took up what was left over of broken pieces, seven large baskets.
en.B: Everyone ate and had plenty. Then they collected the leftover pieces, enough to fill seven large baskets.
en.R: All the people ate as much as they wanted. Then the followers picked up the pieces that were left. They filled seven big baskets.

es.L: Y comieron y quedaron saciados, y recogieron lo sobrante de los trozos: siete cestos grandes.
es.B: Todos comieron hasta quedar satisfechos. Luego recogieron los trozos que sobraron, y llenaron siete cestos grandes.
es.R: Toda la gente comió todo lo que quiso. Después los discípulos recogieron los pedazos que sobraron. Llenaron siete cestos grandes.

sw.L: Nao wakala, wakashiba, wakaokota mabaki ya vipande, vikapu vikubwa saba.
sw.B: Wote walikula, wakashiba. Kisha wakakusanya vipande vilivyobaki, vikajaa vikapu vikubwa saba.
sw.R: Watu wote walikula kadiri walivyotaka. Kisha wanafunzi wakaokota vipande vilivyobaki. Wakajaza vikapu vikubwa saba.

decisions.choice: large baskets: big woven baskets or hampers
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the basket of 6:43 and 8:19. It names a larger basket, big enough to let a man down in it over a wall (Acts 9:25). Jesus keeps the two words apart in 8:19-20.

decisions.choice: satisfied: fed until full
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 6:42 and 8:4.

decisions.choice: large baskets (L, B); big baskets (R)
decisions.reason: The size is part of the meaning of the word. All three levels mark it so that readers can tell these baskets from those of 6:43.

decisions.choice: cestos grandes (here and 8:20); canastas (8:19)
decisions.reason: Mark uses two words for the baskets of the two feedings, the ordinary carrying basket and the large hamper (meaning decision m1). Spanish keeps them apart at every level, as the English "baskets" and "large baskets" do.

decisions.choice: vikapu vikubwa (here and 8:20); vikapu (8:19)
decisions.reason: Mark uses two words for the baskets of the two feedings, the ordinary carrying basket and the large hamper (meaning decision m1). Swahili keeps them apart at every level, as the English "baskets" and "large baskets" do.

source.text: ἦσαν δὲ ὡς τετρακισχίλιοι.

records.literal_gloss: There were now about four thousand.

en.L: Now they were about 4,000.
en.B: There were about 4,000 people.
en.R: About 4,000 people were there.

es.L: Y eran como 4000.
es.B: Eran unas 4000 personas.
es.R: Allí había unas 4000 personas.

sw.L: Nao walikuwa kama elfu nne.
sw.B: Walikuwa watu wapatao elfu nne.
sw.R: Watu wapatao elfu nne walikuwa pale.

decisions.choice: about 4,000: the whole crowd
decisions.reason: Unlike 6:44, the Greek here does not use the word for adult men. It simply counts the crowd.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add the noun that English needs. They use people, since the Greek gives no word for men here.

source.text: καὶ ἀπέλυσεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And he sent away them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them away.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them on their way.
en.R: Then Jesus sent them home.

es.L: Y los despidió.
es.B: Luego los despidió.
es.R: Después Jesús los mandó a sus casas.

sw.L: Naye akawaaga.
sw.B: Kisha akawaaga waende zao.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaaga waende nyumbani.

decisions.choice: sent away: dismissed the crowd to go home
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 8:3. Now they have eaten and can go home.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐμβὰς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Δαλμανουθά.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately having embarked into the boat with the disciples of him he came into the parts of Dalmanutha.

en.L: And immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and came into the region of Dalmanutha.
en.B: At once {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} boarded the boat with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and came to the area of Dalmanutha.
en.R: Right away Jesus got into the boat with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. They went to a place called Dalmanutha.

es.L: Y en seguida, subiendo a la barca con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, fue a la región de Dalmanuta.
es.B: Enseguida subió a la barca con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y fue a la zona de Dalmanuta.
es.R: Jesús subió enseguida a la barca con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Fueron a un lugar llamado Dalmanuta.

sw.L: Na mara, akiisha kupanda mashua pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akaja sehemu za Dalmanutha.
sw.B: Mara alipanda mashua pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akaenda eneo la Dalmanutha.
sw.R: Mara moja Yesu aliingia katika mashua pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Wakaenda mahali paitwapo Dalmanutha.

decisions.choice: Dalmanutha: a place by the lake not known from any other source
decisions.reason: No other ancient writing names Dalmanutha, and where it lay is not known. It was most likely on the west shore of the lake, in Jewish territory, since Pharisees meet Jesus there (8:11).

decisions.choice: Dalmanutha, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read Magadan or Magdala, the names found in the manuscripts of Matthew 15:39. Scribes probably replaced an unknown place with a known one. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a place called Dalmanutha
decisions.reason: Readable signals that Dalmanutha is a place name.

source.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν αὐτῷ, ζητοῦντες παρ’ αὐτοῦ σημεῖον ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, πειράζοντες αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And went out the Pharisees and began to argue with him, seeking from him a sign from the heaven, testing him.

en.L: And the Pharisees went out and began to argue with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, seeking from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a sign from heaven, testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The Pharisees came out and started to dispute with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They demanded a sign from heaven, to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the test.
en.R: The Pharisees came out to argue with Jesus. They wanted to test {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a sign from heaven to prove that God had sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y salieron los fariseos y se pusieron a disputar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, buscando de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} una señal del cielo, para ponerlo a prueba.
es.B: Los fariseos salieron a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} encuentro y se pusieron a debatir con Jesús. Para ponerlo a prueba, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} exigieron una señal del cielo.
es.R: Los fariseos fueron a discutir con Jesús. Querían ponerlo a prueba. Por eso {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pidieron una señal del cielo para probar que Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había enviado.

sw.L: Na Mafarisayo walitoka, wakaanza kubishana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, wakitafuta {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} ishara ya kutoka mbinguni, wakimtega.
sw.B: Mafarisayo walikuja, wakaanza kubishana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. Walidai awaonyeshe ishara kutoka mbinguni ili wamjaribu.
sw.R: Mafarisayo walimjia Yesu ili kubishana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. Walitaka kumjaribu, kwa hiyo wakamwomba ishara kutoka mbinguni ili kuthibitisha kwamba Mungu ndiye aliyemtuma.

decisions.choice: sign: a sign that would prove God was with him
decisions.reason: In Mark a sign is not one of Jesus' healings, which Mark calls works of power. It is a proof, given on demand, that God backs his claims. Israel asked such signs of God in the wilderness and was blamed for testing him (Psalm 95:8-9).

decisions.choice: from heaven: from God
decisions.reason: Heaven stands for God himself. The sign would come from the sky, but the point is that God gives it.

decisions.choice: testing: trying to trap him or prove him false
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Satan's testing in 1:13. They want him to fail.

decisions.choice: sign
decisions.reason: Sign is a key term and keeps the same word at every level. Readable explains what the sign was meant to prove.

source.text: καὶ ἀναστενάξας τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ λέγει· Τί ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ζητεῖ σημεῖον;

records.literal_gloss: And having sighed deeply in the spirit of him he says, Why the generation this seeks a sign?

en.L: And sighing deeply in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "Why does this generation seek a sign?
en.B: He groaned from deep within and said, "Why does this generation look for a sign?
en.R: Jesus let out a deep groan and said, "Why do the people of today keep asking for a sign?

es.L: Y suspirando hondamente en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} espíritu, dice: «¿Por qué busca esta generación una señal?
es.B: Gimió desde lo más hondo de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ser y dijo: «¿Por qué esta generación pide una señal?
es.R: Jesús soltó un profundo gemido y dijo: «¿Por qué la gente de hoy sigue pidiendo una señal?

sw.L: Naye akiugua sana rohoni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, anasema, "Kwa nini kizazi hiki kinatafuta ishara?
sw.B: Aliugua kutoka ndani kabisa ya moyo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akasema, "Kwa nini kizazi hiki kinataka ishara?
sw.R: Yesu alitoa sauti ya kuugua sana, akasema, "Kwa nini watu wa leo wanaendelea kuomba ishara?

decisions.choice: sighed deeply: groaned from the heart
decisions.reason: The verb is stronger than the sigh of 7:34. It shows grief and frustration at their unbelief.

decisions.choice: in his spirit: in his own inner self
decisions.reason: This is Jesus' own spirit, the deepest part of him, as in 2:8.

decisions.choice: this generation: the people of this time, seen as unwilling to believe
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls the wilderness generation that tested God (Deuteronomy 32:5, 32:20; Psalm 95:10). It comes again in 8:38 and 9:19.

decisions.choice: the people of today
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the word means the people living now.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ δοθήσεται τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ σημεῖον.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you, if will be given to the generation this a sign.

en.L: Truly I say to you, no sign will be given to this generation."
en.B: Truly I tell you, this generation will be given no sign at all."
en.R: I tell you the truth: God will not give them a sign. Never!"

es.L: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: a esta generación no se le dará señal alguna».
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que a esta generación no se le dará ninguna señal».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: Dios no les dará ninguna señal. ¡Nunca!».

sw.L: Kweli nawaambia, ishara haitapewa kizazi hiki."
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, hakuna ishara yoyote itakayotolewa kwa kizazi hiki."
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: Mungu hatawapa ishara. Kamwe!"

decisions.choice: if ... a sign: an oath meaning certainly no sign will be given
decisions.reason: This is a Hebrew way of swearing an oath. The full form is "may God punish me if ...", which means "it will certainly not happen" (Psalm 95:11). Jesus denies the demand in the strongest terms.

decisions.choice: will be given: God is the unnamed giver
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God unnamed, as Jewish speech often did.

decisions.choice: no
decisions.reason: Even Literal gives the sense of the oath, since "if" alone would read as an unfinished sentence in English.

decisions.choice: God will not give them a sign. Never!
alternatives: no sign will be given to this generation
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver and shows the force of the oath with a separate word.

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament rendering of the single amen. "De cierto" is the older form and now sounds dated.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament rendering of the single amen, matching John's "Kweli kweli nawaambia" for the double form. Readable says "I tell you the truth", as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς πάλιν ἐμβὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πέραν.

records.literal_gloss: And having left them, again having embarked he went away to the other side.

en.L: And leaving them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} again got into [the boat] and went away to the other side.
en.B: Leaving them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat again and went off to the far shore.
en.R: Then Jesus left them. He got back into the boat and went across the lake.

es.L: Y dejándolos, subiendo otra vez [a la barca], se fue a la otra orilla.
es.B: Los dejó, subió otra vez a la barca y se fue a la otra orilla.
es.R: Entonces Jesús los dejó. Volvió a subir a la barca y cruzó al otro lado del lago.

sw.L: Naye akawaacha, akapanda tena [mashua], akaondoka kwenda ng'ambo.
sw.B: Aliwaacha, akapanda tena mashua, akaenda ng'ambo.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliwaacha. Akapanda tena mashua, akavuka ziwa.

decisions.choice: having left them: Jesus turns his back on the dispute
alternatives: he left them behind by accident
decisions.reason: Leaving them is his answer to their demand.

decisions.choice: the other side: the east shore of the lake
alternatives: another town on the same shore
decisions.reason: They cross back toward the north-east, where they reach Bethsaida (8:22).

decisions.choice: across the lake
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, Readable names the lake.

source.text: Καὶ ἐπελάθοντο λαβεῖν ἄρτους, καὶ εἰ μὴ ἕνα ἄρτον οὐκ εἶχον μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And they forgot to take loaves, and except one loaf not they had with themselves in the boat.

en.L: And they had forgotten to take loaves, and except for one loaf they did not have [any] with them in the boat.
en.B: Now the disciples had forgotten to bring bread. They had just one loaf with them in the boat.
en.R: Jesus' followers had forgotten to bring any food. They had only one loaf of bread with them in the boat.

es.L: Y se habían olvidado de tomar panes, y excepto un pan no tenían [ninguno] consigo en la barca.
es.B: Los discípulos se habían olvidado de llevar pan; solo tenían un pan en la barca.
es.R: Los discípulos de Jesús se habían olvidado de llevar comida. Solo tenían un pan en la barca.

sw.L: Nao walikuwa wamesahau kuchukua mikate, wala hawakuwa na [mikate] pamoja nao katika mashua isipokuwa mkate mmoja.
sw.B: Wanafunzi walikuwa wamesahau kuchukua mikate; walikuwa na mkate mmoja tu ndani ya mashua.
sw.R: Wanafunzi wa Yesu walikuwa wamesahau kuleta chakula. Walikuwa na mkate mmoja tu katika mashua.

decisions.choice: they: the disciples
decisions.reason: The disciples are with Jesus in the boat.

decisions.choice: one loaf: perhaps a hint that Jesus himself is the bread they have
alternatives: only a detail of the story
decisions.reason: Mark mentions the single loaf with care. Some read it as pointing to Jesus, who is with them in the boat. Mark does not say so.

decisions.choice: the disciples (B); Jesus' followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, since the last people named are the Pharisees.

source.text: καὶ διεστέλλετο αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁρᾶτε, βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῆς ζύμης Ἡρῴδου.

records.literal_gloss: And he was instructing them saying, Watch, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was instructing them, saying, "Watch, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod."
en.B: He gave them a warning: "Be careful! Watch out for the Pharisees' yeast and Herod's yeast."
en.R: Jesus warned them, "Be careful! Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and of Herod."

es.L: Y les advertía, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} atentos, {{plural_you:cuídense|cuidaos}} de la levadura de los fariseos y de la levadura de Herodes».
es.B: Les dio esta advertencia: «¡{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado! {{plural_you:Cuídense|Cuidaos}} de la levadura de los fariseos y de la de Herodes».
es.R: Jesús les advirtió: «¡{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado! {{plural_you:Cuídense|Cuidaos}} de la levadura de los fariseos y de Herodes».

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akiwaonya, akisema, "Tazameni, muwe macho dhidi ya chachu ya Mafarisayo na chachu ya Herode."
sw.B: Aliwaonya, "Kuweni waangalifu! Jilindeni na chachu ya Mafarisayo na chachu ya Herode."
sw.R: Yesu aliwaonya, "Kuweni waangalifu! Jihadharini na chachu ya Mafarisayo na ya Herode."

decisions.choice: leaven: a bit of old fermented dough used to make new dough rise
decisions.reason: A small piece of old dough spread through a whole batch. In the Scriptures it often stands for a corrupting influence that spreads (1 Corinthians 5:6-8; Exodus 12:15).

decisions.choice: the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod: their unbelief and hostility
decisions.reason: Mark does not explain the picture. The Pharisees have just demanded a sign (8:11), and Herod killed John (6:14-29). The two groups plotted together against Jesus in 3:6. What they share is a refusal to see who Jesus is.

decisions.choice: Herod: Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee
decisions.reason: The same Herod as in 6:14-29.

decisions.choice: Herod, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "the Herodians", the party of 3:6. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: yeast
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the everyday word. Readable keeps the picture, since the disciples' mistake in the next verses depends on it.

decisions.choice: levadura (every level)
decisions.reason: English uses "leaven" at Literal and "yeast" at Balanced and Readable. Spanish "levadura" covers both, and is the word for the picture of an influence that spreads through the whole (meaning decisions m1, m2).

decisions.choice: chachu (every level)
decisions.reason: English uses "leaven" at Literal and "yeast" at Balanced and Readable. Swahili "chachu" is the leaven that works through dough, the picture of an influence that spreads (meaning decisions m1, m2); "hamira" is the bought baking yeast.

source.text: καὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἀλλήλους ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And they were reasoning with one another that loaves not they have.

en.L: And they were discussing with one another that they have no loaves.
en.B: They began to talk it over among themselves: they had no bread.
en.R: The followers talked among themselves. They thought Jesus said this because they had not brought any bread.

es.L: Y discutían unos con otros que no tienen panes.
es.B: Ellos se pusieron a comentarlo entre sí: no tenían pan.
es.R: Los discípulos hablaron entre ellos. Pensaban que Jesús decía eso porque no habían traído pan.

sw.L: Nao wakawa wakijadiliana wao kwa wao kwamba hawana mikate.
sw.B: Walianza kujadiliana wao kwa wao: hawakuwa na mkate.
sw.R: Wanafunzi walizungumza wao kwa wao. Walifikiri Yesu amesema hivyo kwa sababu hawakuleta mkate.

decisions.choice: that they have no loaves: their talk was about having no bread
decisions.reason: The small word can give the content of their talk or its cause. Either way they think Jesus is speaking about real bread.

decisions.choice: they have, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: we have, as their own words
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "saying" and read "we have", making it direct speech. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: they thought Jesus said this because
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the disciples misunderstood the warning about yeast.

source.text: καὶ γνοὺς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχετε;

records.literal_gloss: And having known he says to them, Why are you reasoning that loaves not you have?

en.L: And knowing [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Why are you discussing that you have no loaves?
en.B: Jesus knew what they were saying, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Why are you talking about having no bread?
en.R: Jesus knew what they were talking about. He said to them, "Why are you talking about not having bread?

es.L: Y conociéndo[lo], les dice: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:discuten|discutís}} que no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} panes?
es.B: Jesús se dio cuenta de lo que decían y les dijo: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:hablan|habláis}} de que no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} pan?
es.R: Jesús sabía de qué estaban hablando. Les dijo: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:hablan|habláis}} de que no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} pan?

sw.L: Naye akijua [hilo], anawaambia, "Kwa nini mnajadiliana kwamba hamna mikate?
sw.B: Yesu alijua walichokuwa wakisema, akawaambia, "Kwa nini mnazungumza juu ya kutokuwa na mkate?
sw.R: Yesu alijua walichokuwa wakizungumza. Akawaambia, "Kwa nini mnazungumza juu ya kukosa mkate?

decisions.choice: knowing it: he was aware of their talk
decisions.reason: Mark does not say how he knew. In 2:8 Jesus knows people's thoughts in his spirit.

decisions.choice: why: a rebuke, not a request for information
decisions.reason: This and the questions that follow scold the disciples for missing the point.

source.text: οὔπω νοεῖτε οὐδὲ συνίετε;

records.literal_gloss: Not yet do you perceive nor understand?

en.L: Do you not yet perceive or understand?
en.B: Do you still not see it or understand?
en.R: Do you still not understand?

es.L: ¿Todavía no {{plural_you:perciben|percibís}} ni {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}?
es.B: ¿Todavía no {{plural_you:ven|veis}} ni {{plural_you:comprenden|comprendéis}}?
es.R: ¿Todavía no {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}?

sw.L: Bado hamtambui wala hamwelewi?
sw.B: Bado hamwoni wala hamwelewi?
sw.R: Bado hamwelewi?

decisions.choice: perceive, understand: the words of Isaiah 6:9-10, used of outsiders in 4:12
decisions.reason: In 4:12 Jesus used these words of those outside, who see but do not perceive. Now he asks whether his own disciples are in the same state.

decisions.choice: understand
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two verbs, which mean nearly the same, into one plain word.

source.text: πεπωρωμένην ἔχετε τὴν καρδίαν ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: Hardened have you the heart of you?

en.L: Do you have your heart hardened?
en.B: Have your hearts been hardened?
en.R: Are your hearts so hard that you cannot understand?

es.L: ¿Endurecido {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} el corazón?
es.B: ¿Se {{plural_you:les|os}} ha endurecido el corazón?
es.R: ¿Tan duro {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} el corazón que no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} entender?

sw.L: Je, moyo wenu umefanywa mgumu?
sw.B: Je, mioyo yenu imekuwa migumu?
sw.R: Je, mioyo yenu ni migumu kiasi kwamba hamwezi kuelewa?

decisions.choice: hardened: dull and closed to understanding
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thinking. Mark said this of the disciples after Jesus walked on the water (6:52), and of Jesus' opponents in 3:5.

decisions.choice: so hard that you cannot understand
decisions.reason: Readable says what a hard heart means here, as at 6:52.

source.text: ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες οὐ βλέπετε καὶ ὦτα ἔχοντες οὐκ ἀκούετε;

records.literal_gloss: Eyes having not do you see, and ears having not do you hear?

en.L: Having eyes, do you not see, and having ears, do you not hear?
en.B: You have eyes; can you not see? You have ears; can you not hear?
en.R: You have eyes, but you do not see! You have ears, but you do not hear!

es.L: Ojos teniendo, ¿no {{plural_you:ven|veis}}?, y oídos teniendo, ¿no {{plural_you:oyen|oís}}?
es.B: {{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} ojos, ¿y no {{plural_you:ven|veis}}? {{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} oídos, ¿y no {{plural_you:oyen|oís}}?
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} ojos, pero no {{plural_you:ven|veis}}! ¡{{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} oídos, pero no {{plural_you:oyen|oís}}!

sw.L: Mkiwa na macho, hamwoni? Na mkiwa na masikio, hamsikii?
sw.B: Mna macho, je, hamwezi kuona? Mna masikio, je, hamwezi kusikia?
sw.R: Mna macho, lakini hamwoni kitu! Mna masikio, lakini hamsikii kitu!

decisions.choice: eyes that do not see, ears that do not hear: the prophets' charge against Israel
decisions.reason: The words recall Jeremiah 5:21 and Ezekiel 12:2, where God's people have eyes and ears but will not use them. They also echo 4:9 and 4:12. The healings of a deaf man (7:31-37) and a blind man (8:22-26) stand on either side of this scene.

decisions.choice: statements instead of questions
decisions.reason: The questions expect the answer that they do not see or hear. Readable says this plainly.

source.text: καὶ οὐ μνημονεύετε ὅτε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους ἔκλασα εἰς τοὺς πεντακισχιλίους, πόσους κοφίνους κλασμάτων πλήρεις ἤρατε;

records.literal_gloss: And not do you remember, \v 19 when the five loaves I broke for the five thousand, how many baskets of broken pieces full you took up?

en.L: And do you not remember, \v 19 when I broke the five loaves for the 5,000, how many baskets full of broken pieces you took up?"
en.B: Do you not remember? \v 19 When I broke five loaves for the 5,000, how many baskets of leftover pieces did you gather?"
en.R: Do you not remember? \v 19 I broke five loaves of bread for 5,000 people. How many baskets of leftover pieces did you pick up?"

es.L: ¿Y no {{plural_you:recuerdan|recordáis}}, \v 19 cuando partí los cinco panes para los cinco mil, cuántas canastas llenas de trozos {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».
es.B: ¿No {{plural_you:recuerdan|recordáis}}? \v 19 Cuando partí cinco panes para los cinco mil, ¿cuántas canastas de trozos sobrantes {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».
es.R: ¿No {{plural_you:se acuerdan|os acordáis}}? \v 19 Yo partí cinco panes para cinco mil personas. ¿Cuántas canastas de pedazos sobrantes {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».

sw.L: Na hamkumbuki, \v 19 nilipoimega ile mikate mitano kwa ajili ya wale elfu tano, mliokota vikapu vingapi vilivyojaa vipande?"
sw.B: Hamkumbuki? \v 19 Nilipoimega mikate mitano kwa ajili ya watu elfu tano, mlikusanya vikapu vingapi vya vipande vilivyobaki?"
sw.R: Hamkumbuki? \v 19 Niliimega mikate mitano kwa ajili ya watu elfu tano. Mliokota vikapu vingapi vya vipande vilivyobaki?"

decisions.choice: do you not remember: read as running into the question of 8:19
alternatives: a separate question ending at the end of 8:18
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates 8:18 and 8:19 as one question. Some editions end the question at "remember". The sense does not change.

decisions.choice: baskets: the smaller baskets of the first feeding
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the word of 6:43 here and the word for large baskets in 8:20. Mark keeps the two feedings apart.

decisions.choice: I broke: Jesus names himself as the one who provided
decisions.reason: The point of the questions is who fed the crowds, and that he is with them in the boat.

decisions.choice: 5,000 people
decisions.reason: Readable adds people, as English needs a noun. In 6:44 the count was of men.

source.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Δώδεκα.

records.literal_gloss: They say to him, Twelve.

en.L: They say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Twelve."
en.B: "Twelve," they told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: They answered, "Twelve."

es.L: Le dicen: «Doce».
es.B: «Doce», {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron.
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «Doce».

sw.L: Wanamwambia, "Kumi na mbili."
sw.B: "Kumi na mbili," walimwambia.
sw.R: Walijibu, "Kumi na mbili."

decisions.choice: they say: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As in 8:1, the sense is past.

source.text: ὅτε καὶ τοὺς ἑπτὰ εἰς τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους, πόσων σπυρίδων πληρώματα κλασμάτων ἤρατε;

records.literal_gloss: When the seven for the four thousand, of how many large baskets fillings of broken pieces you took up?

en.L: "When [I broke] the seven for the 4,000, how many large baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?"
en.B: "And when I broke seven loaves for the 4,000, how many large baskets of pieces did you gather?"
en.R: "And when I broke seven loaves for 4,000 people, how many big baskets of leftover pieces did you pick up?"

es.L: «Cuando [partí] los siete para los cuatro mil, ¿cuántos cestos grandes llenos de trozos {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».
es.B: «Y cuando partí los siete panes para los cuatro mil, ¿cuántos cestos grandes de trozos {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».
es.R: «Y cuando partí siete panes para cuatro mil personas, ¿cuántos cestos grandes de pedazos sobrantes {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».

sw.L: "Na [nilipoimega] ile saba kwa ajili ya wale elfu nne, mliokota vikapu vikubwa vingapi vilivyojaa vipande?"
sw.B: "Na nilipoimega ile mikate saba kwa ajili ya watu elfu nne, mlikusanya vikapu vikubwa vingapi vya vipande?"
sw.R: "Na nilipoimega mikate saba kwa ajili ya watu elfu nne, mliokota vikapu vikubwa vingapi vya vipande vilivyobaki?"

decisions.choice: when the seven for the 4,000: the verb broke is understood from 8:19
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats the question in short form for the second feeding.

decisions.choice: large baskets: the word of 8:8
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the same word for each meal that Mark used in telling it.

decisions.choice: I broke (L in brackets); loaves (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs the verb and the noun that the short question leaves out.

source.text: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἑπτά.

records.literal_gloss: And they say to him, Seven.

en.L: And they say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Seven."
en.B: "Seven," they said.
en.R: They answered, "Seven."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen: «Siete».
es.B: «Siete», respondieron.
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «Siete».

sw.L: Nao wanamwambia, "Saba."
sw.B: "Saba," walisema.
sw.R: Walijibu, "Saba."

decisions.choice: they say: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As in 8:19, the sense is past.

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Οὔπω συνίετε;

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to them, Not yet do you understand?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Do you not yet understand?"
en.B: He said to them, "And you still do not understand?"
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "And you still do not understand?"

es.L: Y les decía: «¿Todavía no {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}?».
es.B: Les dijo: «¿Y todavía no {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}?».
es.R: Entonces Jesús les dijo: «¿Y todavía no {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}?».

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akiwaambia, "Bado hamwelewi?"
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Na bado hamwelewi?"
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaambia, "Na bado hamwelewi?"

decisions.choice: not yet understand: the disciples have seen but not grasped who Jesus is
alternatives: they do not understand the arithmetic
decisions.reason: The question is left open. The next scenes, the blind man healed in two stages (8:22-26) and Peter's confession (8:29), show their sight beginning to come.

decisions.choice: was saying: an imperfect, he said
decisions.reason: Mark often uses this form for Jesus' sayings. It does not change the sense.

source.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Βηθσαϊδάν.

records.literal_gloss: And they come to Bethsaida.

en.L: And they come to Bethsaida.
en.B: They came to Bethsaida.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers came to the town of Bethsaida.

es.L: Y llegan a Betsaida.
es.B: Llegaron a Betsaida.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos llegaron al pueblo de Betsaida.

sw.L: Nao wanafika Bethsaida.
sw.B: Walifika Bethsaida.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walifika katika mji wa Bethsaida.

decisions.choice: Bethsaida: a fishing town at the north end of the lake
decisions.reason: Bethsaida lay just east of where the Jordan enters the lake. Philip the tetrarch had rebuilt it as a city, but Mark calls it a village (8:23). It was the town Jesus sent the disciples toward in 6:45.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers; the town of
decisions.reason: Readable names who came and says that Bethsaida is a town.

source.text: καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ τυφλὸν καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψηται.

records.literal_gloss: And they bring to him a blind [man] and implore him that him he might touch.

en.L: And they bring to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a blind [man] and beg {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to touch him.
en.B: Some people brought a blind man to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to touch him.
en.R: Some people brought a blind man to Jesus. They begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to touch the man.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} traen un ciego, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplican que lo toque.
es.B: Algunos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trajeron un ciego y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pidieron con insistencia que lo tocara.
es.R: Unas personas llevaron a un ciego a Jesús. Le rogaron que tocara al hombre.

sw.L: Nao wanamletea kipofu, na wanamsihi amguse.
sw.B: Watu fulani walimletea kipofu, wakamwomba sana amguse.
sw.R: Watu fulani walimletea Yesu mtu kipofu. Wakamsihi amguse mtu huyo.

decisions.choice: they bring: people of the town, not the disciples
decisions.reason: The subject is general, as in 7:32.

decisions.choice: touch him: people believed Jesus healed by touch
decisions.reason: Jesus had healed by touch many times (1:41; 5:41; 6:5; 7:33).

decisions.choice: some people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that others, not the disciples, brought the man.

source.text: καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ἐξήνεγκεν αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς κώμης, καὶ πτύσας εἰς τὰ ὄμματα αὐτοῦ, ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ, ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Εἴ τι βλέπεις;

records.literal_gloss: And having taken hold of the hand of the blind [man] he led out him outside the village, and having spit on the eyes of him, having laid the hands on him, he was asking him, If anything you see?

en.L: And taking hold of the blind [man's] hand, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led him out of the village, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spit on his eyes [and] laid [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands on him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked him, "Do you see anything?"
en.B: He took hold of the blind man's hand and took him outside the village. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spat on the man's eyes, laid {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on him, and asked, "Can you see anything?"
en.R: Jesus took the blind man's hand and walked with him out of the village. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spit on the man's eyes and put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on him. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked, "Can you see anything?"

es.L: Y tomando de la mano al ciego, lo sacó fuera de la aldea, y habiendo escupido en sus ojos [y] puesto las manos sobre él, le preguntaba: «¿Ves algo?».
es.B: Tomó de la mano al ciego y lo llevó fuera de la aldea. Luego le escupió en los ojos, le puso las manos encima y le preguntó: «¿Puedes ver algo?».
es.R: Jesús tomó de la mano al ciego y caminó con él hasta fuera del pueblo. Allí le escupió en los ojos y le puso las manos encima. Después le preguntó: «¿Puedes ver algo?».

sw.L: Naye, akiushika mkono wa yule kipofu, akampeleka nje ya kijiji; na baada ya kutema mate machoni pake [na] kuweka mikono juu yake, akamwuliza, "Je, unaona chochote?"
sw.B: Alimshika kipofu mkono, akampeleka nje ya kijiji. Kisha akamtemea mate machoni, akaweka mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu yake, akamwuliza, "Unaweza kuona chochote?"
sw.R: Yesu alimshika mkono yule kipofu, akatembea naye mpaka nje ya kijiji. Huko akamtemea mate machoni, akaweka mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu yake. Kisha akamwuliza, "Unaweza kuona chochote?"

decisions.choice: spit on his eyes: saliva was thought to have healing power
decisions.reason: People in that world used saliva as a remedy. Jesus used it with the deaf man too (7:33). Here it is a touch of care.

decisions.choice: outside the village: Jesus heals him away from the crowd
decisions.reason: As with the deaf man (7:33), the healing takes place in private.

decisions.choice: if you see anything: a direct question
alternatives: an indirect question, he asked him whether he saw anything
decisions.reason: In questions of this time the word for if can introduce a direct question. The SBLGNT prints the words as Jesus' own.

decisions.choice: can you see
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable ask about the man's ability to see, which is the point of the question.

source.text: καὶ ἀναβλέψας ἔλεγεν· Βλέπω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ὅτι ὡς δένδρα ὁρῶ περιπατοῦντας.

records.literal_gloss: And having looked up he was saying, I see the men, for as trees I see walking.

en.L: And looking up, he said, "I see {{gender:people|men}}, for I see [them] like trees, walking."
en.B: The man looked up and said, "I see {{gender:people|men}}, but to me they are like trees moving about."
en.R: The man looked up and said, "I see {{gender:people|men}}! They look like trees that are walking."

es.L: Y alzando la vista, decía: «Veo a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}, pues veo como árboles que caminan».
es.B: El hombre alzó la vista y dijo: «Veo {{gender:personas|hombres}}, pero me parecen árboles que andan».
es.R: El hombre miró y dijo: «¡Veo {{gender:personas|hombres}}! Parecen árboles que caminan».

sw.L: Naye akitazama juu, alikuwa akisema, "Ninaona watu, kwa maana ninawaona kama miti, wakitembea."
sw.B: Yule mtu alitazama juu, akasema, "Ninaona watu, lakini kwangu wanaonekana kama miti inayotembea."
sw.R: Yule mtu alitazama, akasema, "Ninaona watu! Wanaonekana kama miti inayotembea."

decisions.choice: looked up: lifted his eyes, or began to see again
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to look up or to recover sight. Here he looks up and sees only in part.

decisions.choice: I see people, for I see them like trees: he knows they are people only because they move
decisions.reason: The shapes look like trees to him. He can tell they are people because they walk.

decisions.choice: people: human beings in general
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for human beings.

decisions.choice: but
decisions.reason: The small word here explains how he knows they are people. In English it reads more clearly as a contrast.

decisions.choice: watu, with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Swahili "watu" already means people, men and women, and the only other wording, "wanaume", means males, so the setting has nothing to change. The same in verses 27, 33 and 34-38.

source.text: εἶτα πάλιν ἐπέθηκεν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ διέβλεψεν καὶ ἀπεκατέστη καὶ ἐνέβλεπεν τηλαυγῶς ἅπαντα.

records.literal_gloss: Then again he laid the hands on the eyes of him, and he saw clearly and he was restored, and he was seeing clearly all things.

en.L: Then again {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} laid [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands on his eyes, and he looked intently and was restored, and he saw everything clearly.
en.B: Then Jesus laid {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on the man's eyes once more. The man looked hard, his sight came back, and he could see everything clearly.
en.R: Then Jesus put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on the man's eyes again. The man looked carefully, and his eyes were healed. Now he could see everything clearly.

es.L: Luego otra vez puso las manos sobre sus ojos, y él miró fijamente y fue restablecido, y veía todo con claridad.
es.B: Entonces Jesús le puso otra vez las manos sobre los ojos. El hombre miró con atención, recobró la vista y podía verlo todo con claridad.
es.R: Luego Jesús volvió a ponerle las manos sobre los ojos. El hombre miró con cuidado, y sus ojos quedaron sanos. Ahora podía ver todo con claridad.

sw.L: Kisha tena akaweka mikono juu ya macho yake, naye akakaza macho, akarudishwa hali yake, akawa akiona vitu vyote waziwazi.
sw.B: Kisha Yesu aliweka tena mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu ya macho ya yule mtu. Yule mtu akakaza macho, kuona kwake kukarudi, naye akaweza kuona kila kitu waziwazi.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliweka tena mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu ya macho ya yule mtu. Yule mtu akatazama kwa makini, na macho yake yakapona. Sasa aliweza kuona kila kitu waziwazi.

decisions.choice: a healing in two stages: a picture of the disciples, who see only in part
decisions.reason: This is the only healing in the Gospels done in two stages. It stands between the disciples' blindness (8:18) and Peter's confession, where Peter sees who Jesus is but not yet that he must suffer (8:29-33). Mark does not explain the link.

decisions.choice: looked intently: looked hard and saw through
decisions.reason: The verb means to see clearly or to stare. The man fixes his eyes and his sight comes back.

decisions.choice: restored: made as he had been
decisions.reason: The same verb as for the withered hand (3:5).

decisions.choice: he saw: he went on seeing
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense shows his sight lasted.

decisions.choice: Jesus (B, R); the man (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name each person, since the Greek uses he for both.

source.text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκον αὐτοῦ λέγων· Μηδὲ εἰς τὴν κώμην εἰσέλθῃς.

records.literal_gloss: And he sent him to [the] home of him, saying, Not even into the village may you enter.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent him to his home, saying, "Do not even enter the village."
en.B: Jesus sent him off home, telling him, "Do not even set foot in the village."
en.R: Jesus sent him home. He told him, "Do not even go back into the village."

es.L: Y lo envió a su casa, diciendo: «Ni siquiera entres en la aldea».
es.B: Jesús lo mandó a su casa y le dijo: «Ni siquiera pongas un pie en la aldea».
es.R: Jesús lo mandó a su casa. Le dijo: «Ni siquiera vuelvas a entrar en el pueblo».

sw.L: Naye akamtuma nyumbani kwake, akisema, "Usiingie hata kijijini."
sw.B: Yesu alimruhusu aende nyumbani kwake, akimwambia, "Usikanyage hata kijijini."
sw.R: Yesu alimrudisha nyumbani. Akamwambia, "Usirudi hata kijijini."

decisions.choice: do not even enter the village, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: do not enter the village nor tell anyone in the village
go to your home, and do not tell anyone in the village
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add or substitute "and do not tell anyone in the village", which makes plain the command to keep quiet found in 1:44, 5:43 and 7:36. The shorter reading is found in early manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: not even: he is to go straight home
alternatives: he may never return to the village
decisions.reason: Jesus keeps the healing quiet, as in 7:36. The man is not to pass through the village on the way.

decisions.choice: go back into
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the man came from the village.

source.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς κώμας Καισαρείας τῆς Φιλίππου· καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἐπηρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων αὐτοῖς· Τίνα με λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι;

records.literal_gloss: And went out Jesus and the disciples of him into the villages of Caesarea of Philip; and on the road he was asking the disciples of him saying to them, Whom me do say the men to be?

en.L: And Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples went out into the villages of Caesarea Philippi; and on the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, saying to them, "Who do {{gender:people|men}} say that I am?"
en.B: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples set out for the villages of the Caesarea Philippi area. As they went, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "Who do {{gender:people|men}} say I am?"
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers went to the villages near the city of Caesarea Philippi. As they walked, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "Who do people say I am?"

es.L: Y salió Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos hacia las aldeas de Cesarea de Filipo; y en el camino preguntaba a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, diciéndoles: «¿Quién {{gender:dice la gente|dicen los hombres}} que soy yo?».
es.B: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos se pusieron en camino hacia las aldeas de la región de Cesarea de Filipo. Mientras iban de camino, les preguntó: «¿Quién {{gender:dice la gente|dicen los hombres}} que soy yo?».
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos fueron a las aldeas que estaban cerca de la ciudad de Cesarea de Filipo. Mientras caminaban, Jesús les preguntó: «¿Quién dice la gente que soy yo?».

sw.L: Na Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walitoka kwenda vijiji vya Kaisaria Filipi; na njiani alikuwa akiwauliza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akiwaambia, "Watu wanasema {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni nani?"
sw.B: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walianza safari kwenda vijiji vya eneo la Kaisaria Filipi. Walipokuwa njiani, aliwauliza, "Watu husema {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni nani?"
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikwenda katika vijiji vilivyo karibu na mji wa Kaisaria Filipi. Walipokuwa wakitembea, aliwauliza, "Watu wanasema {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni nani?"

decisions.choice: Caesarea Philippi: a city at the foot of Mount Hermon, north of the lake
decisions.reason: Philip the tetrarch rebuilt the town and named it for Caesar. It was called Philip's to tell it apart from Caesarea by the sea. It lay in mostly Gentile country at the source of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: on the way: the road becomes the setting for Jesus' teaching
decisions.reason: From here to 10:52 Jesus teaches the disciples on the way to Jerusalem, and the word recurs (9:33; 10:32; 10:52).

decisions.choice: people: people in general
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for human beings.

decisions.choice: the villages of the area (B); the villages near the city of (R)
decisions.reason: The villages belonged to the area of the city. Readable adds that Caesarea Philippi was a city.

decisions.choice: {{gender:dice la gente|dicen los hombres}}
decisions.reason: As the English offers "people" or "men". The span takes in the verb, because "la gente" is singular and "los hombres" plural. Readable says "la gente", as the English Readable says "people".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}
decisions.reason: The English marks no span on "I". Swahili needs the free pronoun "mimi" here, and when Jesus speaks of himself a free pronoun takes the setting, as in John. The same in verse 29.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες ὅτι Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, καὶ ἄλλοι Ἠλίαν, ἄλλοι δὲ ὅτι εἷς τῶν προφητῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him saying that, John the Baptist, and others Elijah, others but that one of the prophets.

en.L: And they told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; but others, one of the prophets."
en.B: They answered, "Some say John the Baptist; some, Elijah; and others, one of the prophets."
en.R: They answered, "Some people say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are John the Baptist. Others say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are Elijah. And others say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are one of the prophets."

es.L: Y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron, diciendo: «Juan el Bautista; y otros, Elías; y otros, que uno de los profetas».
es.B: Ellos respondieron: «Unos dicen que Juan el Bautista; otros, que Elías; y otros, que uno de los profetas».
es.R: Ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} contestaron: «Algunos dicen que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres Juan el Bautista. Otros dicen que eres Elías. Y otros dicen que eres uno de los profetas».

sw.L: Nao wakamwambia, wakisema, "Yohana Mbatizaji; na wengine, Eliya; lakini wengine, mmoja wa manabii."
sw.B: Walimjibu, "Wengine husema ni Yohana Mbatizaji; wengine, Eliya; na wengine, mmoja wa manabii."
sw.R: Walimjibu, "Watu wengine husema {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Yohana Mbatizaji. Wengine husema ni Eliya. Na wengine husema ni mmoja wa manabii."

decisions.choice: the same opinions Herod heard in 6:14-15
decisions.reason: The answers repeat the views of 6:14-15 almost word for word.

decisions.choice: Elijah: the prophet promised to return before the day of the Lord
decisions.reason: Malachi 4:5. See 6:15.

decisions.choice: some people say you are
decisions.reason: Readable writes each answer as a full sentence.

source.text: καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι;

records.literal_gloss: And he was asking them, You but whom me do you say to be?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "But you, who do you say that I am?"
en.B: "And you," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "who do you say I am?"
en.R: Then Jesus asked them, "But what about you? Who do you say I am?"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les preguntaba: «Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, ¿quién {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} que soy yo?».
es.B: «Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} —les preguntó—, ¿quién {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} que soy yo?».
es.R: Entonces Jesús les preguntó: «¿Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}? ¿Quién {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} que soy yo?».

sw.L: Naye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alikuwa akiwauliza, "Lakini ninyi, mnasema {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni nani?"
sw.B: Kisha aliwauliza, "Na ninyi je, mnasema {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni nani?"
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliwauliza, "Na ninyi je? Mnasema {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni nani?"

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, set against people
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first: but you, unlike them.

decisions.choice: he: emphatic, he himself
decisions.reason: Mark adds the pronoun as Jesus turns the question on the disciples.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός.

records.literal_gloss: Answering Peter says to him, You are the Christ.

en.L: Peter answers and says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}."
en.B: Peter answered, "You are {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}."
en.R: Peter answered, "You are {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the King God promised to send!"

es.L: Respondiendo Pedro, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice: «Tú eres el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}».
es.B: Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondió: «Tú eres el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}».
es.R: Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondió: «¡Tú eres el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Rey que Dios prometió enviar!».

sw.L: Petro anajibu, anamwambia, "Wewe ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}."
sw.B: Petro alijibu, "Wewe ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}."
sw.R: Petro alijibu, "Wewe ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mfalme ambaye Mungu aliahidi kumtuma!"

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Anointed One, the king God promised to send
decisions.reason: The word means anointed. Kings of Israel were anointed with oil, and the prophets promised a king from David's line who would set God's people free (2 Samuel 7:12-16; Isaiah 11:1-5). Mark used the title at 1:1.

decisions.choice: Peter's confession: the first time a disciple names Jesus as the Christ
decisions.reason: This is the turning point of Mark's Gospel. Peter sees who Jesus is, but the next verses show he does not yet see what kind of Christ he is (8:31-33).

decisions.choice: the King God promised to send
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title briefly.

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, with the article outside the span
decisions.reason: Spanish says "el Cristo" as naturally as "el Mesías" when the word is a title in a confession, so the article stays outside the span at every level, where the English Balanced and Readable move "the" inside.

source.text: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And he warned them that no one they should tell about him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} warned them that they should tell no one about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He gave them strict orders not to tell anyone about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then Jesus strictly told them not to tell anyone who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.

es.L: Y les advirtió severamente que a nadie hablaran de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Les dio órdenes estrictas de no hablar de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a nadie.
es.R: Entonces Jesús les mandó con firmeza que no le dijeran a nadie quién era.

sw.L: Naye akawaonya vikali wasimwambie mtu yeyote habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.B: Aliwaagiza kwa mkazo wasimwambie mtu yeyote habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliwakataza kabisa wasimwambie mtu yeyote {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni nani.

decisions.choice: warned: gave a stern command
decisions.reason: This is the same verb used for Peter rebuking Jesus and Jesus rebuking Peter (8:32-33), and for Jesus silencing demons (1:25; 3:12). Here it is a strict order.

decisions.choice: tell no one: the title must not be spread until its meaning is clear
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny the title. People would hear it as a call to war against Rome. He begins at once to teach what kind of Christ he is (8:31).

source.text: Καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς ὅτι δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστῆναι·

records.literal_gloss: And he began to teach them that it is necessary the Son of Man many things to suffer and to be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes and to be killed and after three days to rise;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes and be killed and after three days rise again;
en.B: He then began teaching them that the Son of Man had to undergo great suffering, be rejected by elders, chief priests and scribes, be put to death, and rise again after three days.
en.R: Then Jesus began to teach {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. He said that the Son of Man must go through many terrible sufferings. The leaders of the people, the leading priests and the teachers of God's law would reject {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He would be killed, but after three days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would come back to life.

es.L: Y comenzó a enseñarles que es necesario que el Hijo del Hombre padezca mucho y sea rechazado por los ancianos y los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas, y que sea muerto y después de tres días resucite.
es.B: Entonces comenzó a enseñarles que el Hijo del Hombre tenía que sufrir mucho y ser rechazado por los ancianos, los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas; que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matarían y que después de tres días resucitaría.
es.R: Luego Jesús comenzó a enseñar a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Les dijo que el Hijo del Hombre tenía que pasar por muchos sufrimientos terribles. Los líderes del pueblo, los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} rechazarían. Lo matarían, pero después de tres días volvería a la vida.

sw.L: Naye akaanza kuwafundisha kwamba ni lazima Mwana wa Adamu ateswe mengi, akataliwe na wazee na wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi, auawe, na baada ya siku tatu afufuke.
sw.B: Kisha alianza kuwafundisha kwamba ilimlazimu Mwana wa Adamu kupata mateso mengi, kukataliwa na wazee, wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi, kuuawa, na baada ya siku tatu kufufuka.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alianza kuwafundisha wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Alisema kwamba ni lazima Mwana wa Adamu apitie mateso mengi ya kutisha. Viongozi wa watu, wakuu wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria wangemkataa. Angeuawa, lakini baada ya siku tatu angefufuka.

decisions.choice: must: it is God's purpose, found in the Scriptures
decisions.reason: The word means it is necessary. In Mark the need comes from God's plan, written beforehand (9:12; 14:21, 14:49).

decisions.choice: rejected: the word of Psalm 118:22
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the stone the builders rejected in Psalm 118:22, which Jesus quotes in 12:10.

decisions.choice: elders, chief priests, scribes: the three groups of the Jewish council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Together they made up the Sanhedrin, the ruling council (14:53, 15:1). The chief priests were the high priest and leading priestly families.

decisions.choice: after three days: by the third day, counting in the Jewish way
decisions.reason: In Jewish counting part of a day counted as a day. Mark tells of the resurrection on the third day (16:1-2; compare 14:58, 15:29).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus speaks of himself
decisions.reason: As in 2:10 and 2:28, Jesus uses the title for himself. It recalls the one like a son of man in Daniel 7:13-14.

decisions.choice: the leaders of the people
decisions.reason: Readable explains elders as leaders of the people, and uses teachers of God's law for scribes as in earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre, with capitals and no gender setting
decisions.reason: The title used through Mark, as in John: Jesus speaks of himself (meaning decision m5), so it is never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley (R)
alternatives: los maestros de la ley (every level)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish: "escribas" is the familiar name for these experts in the Law of Moses; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili title, as in John; "Adamu" is also a word for humankind (as in "binadamu"). "Mwana wa Mtu" is more literal but unfamiliar. Never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "waandishi" is the familiar name for these experts in the Law of Moses; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ παρρησίᾳ τὸν λόγον ἐλάλει.

records.literal_gloss: And openly the word he was speaking.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking the word openly.
en.B: He spoke about this quite plainly.
en.R: Jesus told them all this very plainly.

es.L: Y hablaba la palabra abiertamente.
es.B: Hablaba de esto con toda claridad.
es.R: Jesús les dijo todo esto con mucha claridad.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akilinena neno hilo waziwazi.
sw.B: Alizungumza jambo hili waziwazi kabisa.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaeleza mambo haya yote waziwazi.

decisions.choice: openly: plainly, without hiding the meaning
decisions.reason: Until now Jesus has taught in parables and kept his identity hidden. Now he tells the disciples plainly.

decisions.choice: the word: this message about his suffering
decisions.reason: The phrase points back to what he has just taught in 8:31.

source.text: καὶ προσλαβόμενος ὁ Πέτρος αὐτὸν ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken aside Peter him began to rebuke him.

en.L: And Peter took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} aside and began to rebuke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Peter took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to one side and began to rebuke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then Peter took Jesus away from the others and began to tell {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was wrong.

es.L: Y Pedro, tomándolo aparte, comenzó a reprenderlo.
es.B: Pedro {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevó aparte y comenzó a reprenderlo.
es.R: Entonces Pedro se llevó a Jesús lejos de los demás y comenzó a decirle que estaba equivocado.

sw.L: Na Petro akamchukua kando, akaanza kumkemea.
sw.B: Petro alimchukua kando, akaanza kumkemea.
sw.R: Kisha Petro alimchukua Yesu mbali na wengine, akaanza kumwambia kwamba amekosea.

decisions.choice: rebuke: speak sharply to correct
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 8:30 and 8:33. Peter speaks to Jesus as Jesus speaks to demons.

decisions.choice: taken aside: drew him away from the others
decisions.reason: Peter speaks to Jesus privately.

decisions.choice: tell him that he was wrong
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for rebuke.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπιστραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐπετίμησεν Πέτρῳ καὶ λέγει· Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ, ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: And having turned and having seen the disciples of him he rebuked Peter and says, Go behind me, Satan, because not you set your mind on the things of God but the things of the men.

en.L: But turning around and seeing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rebuked Peter and says, "Get behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Satan, because you are not setting your mind on the things of God but on the things of {{gender:people|men}}."
en.B: But Jesus turned and looked at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rebuked Peter. "Get behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Satan!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "Your mind is not on what God cares about, but on what people care about."
en.R: But Jesus turned around and looked at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rebuked Peter. "Get behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Satan!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "You are thinking the way people think, not the way God thinks."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, volviéndose y viendo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, reprendió a Pedro y dice: «Ponte detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, Satanás, porque no piensas en las cosas de Dios, sino en las de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}».
es.B: Pero Jesús se volvió, miró a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y reprendió a Pedro. «¡Ponte detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, Satanás! —le dijo—. Lo que a ti te importa no es lo que le importa a Dios, sino lo que le importa a la gente».
es.R: Pero Jesús se dio vuelta y miró a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Luego reprendió a Pedro. «¡Ponte detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, Satanás! —le dijo—. Tú piensas como piensa la gente, no como piensa Dios».

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, akigeuka na kuwaona wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akamkemea Petro, na anasema, "Kaa nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, Shetani, kwa sababu huyafikiri mambo ya Mungu bali ya wanadamu."
sw.B: Lakini Yesu aligeuka, akawatazama wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akamkemea Petro. Akasema, "Kaa nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, Shetani! Mawazo yako hayako kwenye mambo anayoyajali Mungu, bali kwenye yale wanayoyajali wanadamu."
sw.R: Lakini Yesu aligeuka, akawatazama wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Kisha akamkemea Petro, akasema, "Kaa nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, Shetani! Unafikiri jinsi wanadamu wanavyofikiri, si jinsi Mungu anavyofikiri."
